pr_title: Add FPS compatible option in second mode of the animation editor snapping
pr_body:
- Fixes https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/98609
- ~Supersedes https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/98826~ Now conflict is solved

Makes it optional to snap the FPS to a close integer FPS when in SecondMode.

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4ecc61e0-08ca-4b95-b826-1b6592614449)

Partially revert https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/97569 to disallow fractional FPS because KeyEditor's spin slider syncs with the FPS of the Snap setting, but KeyEditor's spin slider only allows integers, so if fractional FPS is used for snapping, KeyEditor's spin slider will break. Moreover, it is not consistent with this FPS compatible option.

Even if the KeyEditor spin slider allows fractional values, this will still cause problems due to lack of precision[^1], so the fundamental solution is to separate the FPS values for KeyEditor/Timeline from the step(snapping) values. In other words, it means that we need to add a FPS value as well as a step value to the Animation property, but I feel that it should be an editor-only property because it is too specific to the niche case of fractional FPS.

[^1]: Since the value of time in KeyEditor exceeds 10.0 usually, there is a lack of precision if we want to use a step of 0.0625 since it will be like 10.0625 or 100.0625

issue_context.title: Animation editor key snapping is rounded to some predetermined value instead of using exact snap value
issue_context.body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in : 4.4.dev3, 4.4.dev2
- Not reproducible in : 4.2.2.stable

### System information

Windows 11 - Godot v4.4.dev3

### Issue description

When you set time snap value in animation editor and you try to create or move key, the result key time value is rounded to some predetermined value instead of using exact number to snap.
Some examples:
- If snap value is 0.15, key is actually snapped to value 0.1429
- If snap value is 0.225 or 0.275, key is actually snapped to value 0.25
- If snap value is 0.3 or 0.4, key is actually snapped to value 0.3333333...
- If snap value is from 0.45 to 0.75, key is actually snapped to value 0.5
- If snap value is bigger than 0.75, key is actually snapped to value 1
The same rules apply for any integer value like 2.225 is snapped to 2.25, or 4.3 is snapped to 4.33333...

Note that timeline cursor doesn't have this issue and it snaps correctly to exact snap value, no matter how much decimal part is.

### Steps to reproduce

1.) Create AnimationPlayer, some Sprite or ColorRect, and create some simple moving animation for it
2.) Try to set snapping value to 0.25, 0.3, 0.425, 0.45 and 0.75 and try to create new key or move existing one and see that it snaps to incorrect value, while timeline cursor is moving correctly (when timeline cursor snap is enabled)

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[MRP.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/17541034/MRP.zip)

I assume half of this problem is a specification rather than a bug.

When importing an external 3D animation, the default snap value is `1/30`, which is an unreasonable number, `0.0333`.

The problem here is that simple truncation and snapping will not allow snapping to 1.0s, so we use `modf()` snapping with https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/92670 and https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/96328 to snap every 1.0 interval.

So I think there are some possible approaches:

1. Set the default for all animation modes to FPS Mode and prevent snapping to 1.0 when 0.333 is accumulated (allow accumulated error in Second mode)
    - In other words, needs to add a change to #98826 to all animation default to FPS Mode
2. Ignore the accumulation error issue when snapping value greater than 1.0 and document that
    - In other words, #98826 only applies when step is 1.0 or higher and needs to add documentation
3. Implement the "fps compatibility mode toggle" in Second mode in addition to approach 2
    - Disable this mode allows accumulated errors in Second mode when stepping value is less than 1.0

I believe that the default change by approach 1 should not be done, at least not during Godot4 (if we done it, it should do in Godot5 milestone), since it could break projects workflow that use the existing 0.0333 snap. So IMO, we should probably choose approach 2 or 3.

However, since https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/92670 is a change made in 4.3 and not 4.2, it may still be possible to fix with approach 1 it at this time, we will discuss this later in the animation meeting @lyuma @fire.
